notes: at which is read as the whole rendering of the single אֲשֶׁר, headed on which under rule 24; no preposition morpheme stands in the clause, and the competing reading (at added) is named in that unit's note.
The suffix on שֹׁמְעוֹ is the morpheme resuming the antecedent and takes the separately written it, so rule 22's fusion does not reach it (rule 22, closing paragraph).

The suffix on אָזְנָיו is realized by the of linking ears to every one that heareth it, the expression naming its referent, rather than by a possessive pronoun; the competing reading (suffix unrepresented, of added) is named in that unit's note.
